FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A17
A steady red requires you to stay stopped for as long as it is red, whereas after stopping at a flashing red you may go once the way is clear. [A17]
Why it matters: group_hint red-signals; prereq_hint sec04-F06; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec04-F06, sec04-F14.
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A18
A flashing red at a railroad crossing is the exception: you stay stopped until the light stops flashing and the way is clear, even when no train is in sight. [A18]
Why it matters: group_hint red-signals; prereq_hint sec04-R01; difficulty_hint 4; confusable_with sec04-F14, sec04-F15.
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A17
Right on red is allowed after a full stop unless a sign forbids it, but left on red is allowed only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street. [A17]
Why it matters: group_hint turn-on-red; prereq_hint sec04-F06; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec04-F07, sec04-F08.
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A17
A steady yellow means stop safely if you can because red is coming, while you continue carefully only when you are too close to stop safely. [A17]
Why it matters: group_hint yellow-signals; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec04-F09, sec04-F16.
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A18
A steady yellow arrow signals that turn permission is ending, while a flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. [A18]
Why it matters: group_hint yellow-signals; prereq_hint sec04-R04; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec04-F12, sec04-F16.
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A18
A steady red arrow keeps you stopped while it is red, but a flashing red arrow lets you go in its direction after a full stop once traffic and pedestrians are clear. [A18]
Why it matters: group_hint arrows; prereq_hint sec04-F11; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec04-F11, sec04-F17.
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A18
Over a lane, a steady yellow X means get out of the lane, while a flashing yellow X means the lane is shared for left turns. [A18]
Why it matters: group_hint lane-use-signals; prereq_hint sec04-F18; difficulty_hint 4; confusable_with sec04-F20, sec04-F21.
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A17
A dark, non-working signal and a steady red both require a stop at the stop line, crosswalk or intersection edge, but at a dark signal you stay stopped only until it is safe to enter and continue through. [A17]
Why it matters: group_hint signal-failure; prereq_hint sec04-F04; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec04-F04, sec04-F05, sec04-F06.
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A17
A police officer, emergency worker or uniformed school crossing guard can direct you contrary to a signal, but no one may avoid a signal by cutting through private property. [A17]
Why it matters: group_hint control-devices; prereq_hint sec04-F01; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec04-F02, sec04-F03.
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0017]
